title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Introducing Zr or Ti into Ce6-node UiO-66 increases the driving force for ligand-to-metal charge transfer, narrows the gap, and experimentally gives mixed-metal frameworks higher overall-water-splitting activity and lower recombination than single-metal analogues.
explanation: Truhlar’s calculations indicated that UiO-66(Ce) favors LMCT and that Zr or Ti makes the LMCT energy more negative. Melillo’s UiO-66(Zr/Ce/Ti) produced 230 and 110 μmol g−1 H2 and O2 under UV–vis and retained much of that activity under visible light; photoluminescence was weaker than for UiO-66(Zr), consistent with better charge separation. The trimetallic nodes are also described as suited to the four-electron, four-proton water-oxidation demand.
scope: Ce6-based UiO-66 and mixed Zr/Ce/Ti UiO-66 photocatalysts for overall water splitting.
conditions: Xe-lamp UV–vis or visible irradiation in water; repeated use without an obvious activity drop was reported for the trimetallic MOF.
caveats: Transient-absorption inactivation curves of the five UiO-66 samples were similar, so the activity difference is not attributed to that particular kinetic observable.
